capitals.name: Hamdullahi
capitals.note: Ahmadu established the capital there in 1820 (Massina page); 'The capital was established in 1819' (Seku Amadu page); the page puts it northeast of Djenné, just south of modern Mopti, so the point is Mopti's coordinates, and 1818-1819 is the proxy for the years before the city. Levelled by Umar Tall on 16 May 1862.

rulers.name: Seku Amadu (Ahmadu Lobbo)
rulers.note: Died 20 April 1845 (Seku Amadu page); the Massina page text says 1844.

rulers.name: Amadu II (Ahmadu bin Ahmadu Lobbo)
rulers.note: 'ruled over Massina from 1844 to 1852' (Seku Amadu page), which conflicts with the 1845 death of his father.

rulers.name: Amadu III
rulers.note: The ruler table gives 1852, the text 'in 1853'; captured and put to death in 1862.

The outline is the Bamana 1803 outline: it holds Ségou (140 cells), Timbuktu and the Hombori-Seno lands; the Ségou remnant is removed because Ségou stayed Bambara to 1861. region.text: Djenné and Massina, the Inner Niger Delta around Mopti, where Hamdullahi stood

ledger.note: 1818: Seku Amadu founds the Massina Empire. 'It was founded by Seku Amadu in 1818 during the Fulani jihads after defeating the Bambara Empire'; the text has the empire taking Djenné in 1818. His jihad was 'probably continuous from 1810 through 1818' (Seku Amadu page). Noukouma has no year on the Massina page; the Bamana page dates it 1818.

1826/7: Seku Amadu takes Timbuktu. The page: Ahmadu 'in 1826/7 conquered Timbuktu'; Massina firmly controlled Timbuktu from 1833. The Seku Amadu page speaks only of an informal incorporation 'with little resistance'.

ledger.note: The rest of Cliopatria's 1822 outline (Fakala-Kunari, Hayre-Seno, Nabbe-Dude and the Niger bend) is undated on the pages: the Massina page names five regions without years, the Seku Amadu page says the empire extended to the Inner Niger Delta and exerted some authority over Timbuktu, Ségou and Kaarta. Bridged at 1826 with Timbuktu (page silent).
1840: Timbuktu rises. The page: a Tuareg force drove off the garrison in 1840, was defeated in 1841, and in 1842-1844 drove Massina out of Timbuktu.
By 1846: Massina retakes Timbuktu. The page: Massina starved the city back into submission by 1846; Timbuktu rebelled again under Ahmadu II.

wars.name: Fulani jihad of Massina

zones.text: Djenné and Massina, the Inner Niger Delta around Mopti, where Hamdullahi stood

wars.outcome: Seku Amadu defeats the Bambara and takes Djenné and the Mopti country in 1818; the Massina page says a force of 1,000 routed a 100,000-strong army under General Jamogo Seri at Noukouma (no year on that page).
wars.note: Ardo Amadu had mobilised over 200,000 men from Segu and other towns; the page's phrase is that Segu was the overlord of the local Fulbe rulers.

wars.name: Massina-Timbuktu wars
wars.outcome: Massina conquers Timbuktu in 1826/7 and holds it firmly from 1833; the Tuareg drove off the garrison in 1840, lose in 1841, drive Massina out in 1842-1844; Massina starves the city back by 1846. The Seku Amadu page adds a revolt in 1833 that was defeated, ending in a truce under which Fulbe forces would not occupy Timbuktu.
wars.note: The two pages disagree about whether Fulbe forces held Timbuktu in 1833.

notes: Pages opened: two (budget 1-2); the Bamana page opened for bamana-empire also dates Noukouma (1818) and the Bambara end (1861). Neither page gives an area, so no infobox comparison. Cliopatria's 1820-21 shape (41k km2) sits on the Ségou country and its 1822-1860 shape (105k km2) is the Bamana outline of 1803-1819; both are corrected to exclude a 100 km disc at Ségou, which the Bamana page keeps Bambara until 10 March 1861. The remaining land beyond the Djenné-Mopti heartland and Timbuktu enters at 1826 by a confidence-1 bridge. Disagreements: Hamdullahi built 1819 (Seku Amadu page) or 1820 (Massina page); Seku Amadu died 1844 (Massina text) or 20 April 1845 (Seku Amadu page); Amadu III from 1852 (table) or 1853 (text). Pages vs Cliopatria: end 1862 (Cliopatria 1861). Counterparts needing dossiers: tukulor-empire (af-03-x), Tuareg of Timbuktu, the Dogon and Seno lands. Gazetteer lacks Hamdullahi, Noukouma, the Seno plain.
